answer: Sybil resistance comes from bonding each identity in a separate escrow and linking correlated equivocation across them: for k coordinated identities, pairwise evidence creates Θ(k²) penalty exposure, proportional to k(k−1)/2. Upon detection, an exponential capital-loss multiplier can make controlling a swarm disproportionately costly, so splitting stake does not dilute risk. The oasis, comet, and signal labels are examples; consensus relies on verifiable shared faults, not names.
